category_title: Artistically-inclined students who adapt storytelling skills to technical 3D modeling
minimal_context: The student is working in Cinema 4D to model 3D assets and adjust visual optics for a bike delivery game.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at your environment models for your bike delivery game in Cinema 4D. During the peer feedback session, it was mentioned that we need to work on the visual optics.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I got part of the idea for my game since my school is by Fisherman’s Wharf; I go there a lot. I just get to see the environment around there a lot so I know more about how it’s going to be.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That's good. How are you going to set up the models in the software?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I recreated San Francisco landmarks like Fisherman’s Wharf and the Golden Gate Bridge, but I'm having trouble trying to visualize three-dimensional objects in two-dimensional space.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think you should try next to fix that?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't know what to do. A classmate made the observation that some of my early renderings were too flat. I know I'm supposed to use Cinema 4D's lighting tools to include shadows from both the bridge and bike to create a 3D effect, and play with depth of field, but the software is too complicated for me to figure out on my own.
